title: Per-component adaptive token delta & shadow-stack migration plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: introduce an adaptive per-component token delta system plus a deterministic shadow-stack (layered elevation variables) and roll these into the component library with minimal visual regressions. This ticket defines the naming convention, the arithmetic model for deltas, the shadow-stack spec (stacked micro-elevations), rollout plan, migration codemods, and QA criteria for buttons, tables, and charts. Rationale: allow product teams to opt components into denser or airier variants without proliferating discrete token families while improving accessibility contrast and reducing ad-hoc shadow usage in component implementations.
background_and_context: Current problems: (1) teams create bespoke spacing/radius/shadow values to hit visual goals, causing fragmentation; (2) elevation is implemented ad-hoc as single shadow values leading to inconsistent layering across stack contexts; (3) typography scale does not provide explicit delta arithmetic for component-level overrides. This work replaces scattered values with a delta-based overlay system: base tokens + signed delta tokens per component category (e.g., --spacing-base + --spacing-delta-button) and a shadow-stack that composes 3 micro-layers to produce perceptually consistent elevation with accessible contrast checks.
proposal_summary: 1) Define token naming: --rwd-spacing-base, --rwd-spacing-delta-{component}-{size} (signed), --rwd-radius-base, --rwd-radius-delta-{component}, --rwd-elevation-stack-1/2/3 and --rwd-elevation-composite-{level}. 2) Typography: adopt a ratio-based stepper with fractional steps for micro copy (use 1.125 ratio as baseline and allow -0.5/+0.5 fractional steps via delta tokens). 3) Shadow-stack: three alpha-modulated layers (ambient, penumbra, lift) with deterministic composition rules; composite tokens generated at build-time for runtime efficiency. 4) Migration: provide aliases, codemods, and a two-phase rollout (design system beta + canary release + full migration).

design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: - Use delta arithmetic for flexibility vs. fixed token sets for predictability. We accept a small runtime burden (composite tokens generated at build) to avoid runtime calculations in clients. - Shadow-stack uses three layers to balance realism and CSS performance; more layers improve realism but increase style complexity. - Fractional typography steps enable micro-adjustments for data-dense UIs at the cost of slightly more token complexity. - Aliasing strategy: provide compatibility aliases for 6 months then deprecate to encourage migration.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: visual regressions in customer-facing dashboards. Mitigation: canary rollout + visual diffs + strict change thresholds. - Risk: teams misuse delta tokens and create large cumulative deltas. Mitigation: lint rules and CI checks to cap deltas per component. - Risk: increased bundle size from composite tokens. Mitigation: generator produces only needed composite tokens per release and tree-shakes unused ones.
